## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Anantarapaccayakathā* (Kv 14.3) is the third debate of the fourteenth chapter (*vagga*) of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated in the *Abhidhamma Piṭaka*. The text centers on the doctrinal problem of the continuity of the psychic stream (*santati*) and the functioning of contiguous conditioning (*anantarapaccaya*) [Dube 1980]. In this controversy, the Uttarāpathaka school advocated a strictly unbroken, uninterrupted psychic flow, a stance contested by the Theravādins, who utilized the conceptual distinction between latent (*bhavaṅga*) and manifest or functional (*kiriya*) mental states to explain psychological continuity [Dube 1980].
